en.AutoCorrectDesc: Whether the project folder has an autocorrect.txt file: replacements Paratext makes automatically while you type in this project, one per line (text-->replacement).

en.BooksNoneMissing: None missing from GEN to REV: all 66 books are present.

en.CustomStyDesc: Whether the project folder has a custom.sty file: changes to the stylesheet above (new markers or different formatting) for this project only. Paratext applies them on top of the stylesheet.
en.CustomVrsDesc: Whether the project folder has a custom.vrs file: changes to the versification above (different verse counts, mappings, missing verses) for this project only.
en.Description: Shows the project's settings (Settings.xml) as a page in the web browser, with a description of each setting and the characters used in the text. It never changes the project.
en.EmptyLegend: Setting names in yellow are empty (shown when "Show empty settings" is ticked).
en.Error: The report could not be made: {0}
en.FileAbsent: No: the project folder has no {0}.
en.FileUnknown: Not known: Paratext 10 does not let extensions see the project's files. Choose {0} with "Choose files..." to include it.
en.FolderNoSettings: This folder has no Settings.xml, so it is not a Paratext project folder: {0}
en.FolderNotAllowed: Paratext 10 did not allow the folder to be read: {0}
en.FolderNotInRoot: The folder {0} has no folder for the project {1}.
en.FolderReadOnly: The folder can be read but not written to here, so Save will download the file instead.
en.FolderRootWhere: Only once: choose the folder where Paratext 10 keeps its projects, {0}. After that each window finds its project's folder by itself.
en.FolderWrongProject: This is the folder of project {0}, not of the project open here ({1}). Choose the folder {2}.
en.FontMissing: (this font is not installed on this computer)
en.Intro: Each row gives the name of the setting in Settings.xml, its value, and a description. Where it helps, the value is also shown in a more readable form, with the stored text below it.
en.InvalidFoundDesc: Characters of InvalidCharacters that still occur in the text of the {0} books read, with how often each occurs. The checks report them as errors.
en.InvalidFoundName: Disapproved characters found in the text
en.InvalidFoundNone: None: no disapproved character occurs in the text.
en.InvalidLegend: Setting names in orange list disapproved (invalid) items: characters, punctuation, markers or words that the checks report as errors.
en.LookAlikeLegend: Characters that look alike show their Unicode value under them.
en.NoDescription: No description is available for this setting.
en.NoLdml: No language settings file named {0} was found in the project folder.
en.NoProjectFolder: The folder of project {0} could not be found.
en.NotInLanguageDesc: Letters (and letter combinations) approved in ValidCharacters that are not in the Alphabetic characters list of the language settings ({0}, sil:simple). A capitalized combination such as Ch or CH counts as listed when ch is listed.
en.NotInLanguageDescUsed: Letters (and letter combinations) used in the text and approved in ValidCharacters that are not in the Alphabetic characters list of the language settings ({0}, sil:simple), with how often each occurs. A capitalized combination such as Ch or CH counts as listed when ch is listed.
en.NotInLanguageName: Valid characters not in the language settings
en.NotInLanguageNone: None: every letter in ValidCharacters is in the Alphabetic characters list.
en.NotInLanguageNoneUsed: None: every letter used in the text is in the Alphabetic characters list.
en.NotSettings: This is not a Settings.xml file: {0}
en.NoteFiles: Settings from the files you chose: {0}. The book text is read from Paratext 10.
en.NoteP10: Paratext 10 gives extensions only {0} of the project's settings, shown here. For the full report, click "Choose files..." above and pick the project's Settings.xml (and its .ldml language file, custom.sty, custom.vrs and autocorrect.txt) from its folder, for example C:\My Paratext 9 Projects\{1}.
en.OpenProjectFirst: Open a project (not a resource) in a Scripture window first, then choose this command from that window's Tools menu.
en.PasteIntro: If "Choose files..." does not open a file chooser, open the project's Settings.xml in a text editor, copy all of it, and paste it here.
en.PunctFoundDesc: Items of InvalidPunctuation that still occur in the text of the {0} books read, with how often each occurs. The checks report them as errors.
en.PunctFoundName: Disapproved punctuation found in the text
en.PunctFoundNone: None: no disapproved punctuation occurs in the text.
en.PunctNote: _ marks a space or the edge of a word: _( = at the start of a word, )_ = at the end of a word, _-_ = between spaces, - = inside a word.
en.PunctUnusedDesc: Approved punctuation (ValidPunctuation) that does not occur in the text of the {0} books read. It may have been approved in the past and no longer be part of this project.
en.PunctUnusedNone: None: every approved item occurs in the text.
en.PunctUsedDesc: Approved punctuation (punctuation inventory, Language settings) that occurs in the text of the {0} books read, with how often each item occurs. Items are formed as Paratext forms them: _ marks a space or the edge of a word. Approved items that are not used are listed below.
en.ReadOnlyNote: This page only shows the settings. To change them, use Paratext (Project properties, Language settings, Quotation rules, or the inventories).
en.Title: Project Settings Report
en.UnusedDesc: Approved characters (ValidCharacters) that do not occur in the text of the {0} books read. NOTE: this list includes characters that may have been approved in the past and are no longer a part of this project.
en.UnusedName: Approved but not used in the text
en.UnusedNone: None: every approved character occurs in the text.
en.UsedValidDesc: Approved characters (character inventory, Language settings) that occur in the text of the {0} books read, with how often each occurs. Approved characters that are not used are listed below.

fr.OpenProjectFirst: Ouvrez d'abord un projet (pas une ressource) dans une fenêtre de texte biblique, puis choisissez cette commande dans le menu Outils de cette fenêtre.
